chunks: Abū ʿAlī al-Ashʿarī, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Indeed, a man commits a sin and is thereby deprived of salat al-layl, and indeed an evil deed moves more quickly upon its doer than a knife through flesh.

key_terms.الذَّنْبَ: the sin or act of disobedience

ai.seo_question: How do sins affect a person's ability to perform salat al-layl?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that sin has immediate spiritual consequences, including deprivation from the blessing of salat al-layl (night prayer). It also warns that the harmful effects of evil deeds reach the sinner swiftly and deeply.
